What businesses pay for goods and services is rising at the fastest yearly pace in almost four years.

Producer prices rose 0.3% in October and 6.5% over the past 12 months, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Nov 13. That is the biggest 12-month rise since November 2022. Food at the wholesale level jumped 1.3% in one month.

These are the prices businesses pay before anything reaches a store shelf.

My take: wholesale costs are where a lot of what you pay later starts.

Where have you noticed prices creeping up lately?

Source: BLS PPI, October 2026 (released Nov 13 2026)

A 0% balance transfer can save real money, but it is rarely free.

Most cards charge a balance transfer fee, often 3% to 5% of the amount moved, the CFPB says. On a $5,000 balance, that is $150 to $250 up front.

The 0% rate also ends. Whatever is left after the promo period starts charging the card's regular rate.

My take: a transfer works best with a payoff plan that beats the deadline.

Have you ever used a balance transfer? Did it work out?

Source: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau

#CreditCards #Debt #MoneyMyths

Food got more expensive for businesses in October, before it ever reached a shelf.

Wholesale food prices rose 1.3% in one month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Nov 13. That is what producers charge the businesses that sell to you.

Stores do not have to pass that on, and not all of it always shows up. But it is part of what ends up on your receipt.

My take: the grocery bill is where inflation feels most personal.

Which grocery item has gone up most for you?

Source: BLS PPI, October 2026 (released Nov 13 2026)

Filling up got cheaper this month.

The national average for regular gas was $3.90 a gallon on Nov 12, AAA said, the first time below $4 since July. It was $4.10 a week earlier and $4.36 a month earlier.

AAA pointed to lower crude oil prices, cheaper winter-blend fuel and lighter fall demand. It is still well above a year ago.

My take: 46 cents a gallon in a month is real relief for anyone with a long commute.

What are you paying for gas where you live?

Source: AAA, Nov 12 2026

#GasPrices #Gas #CostOfLiving
column6: Source: AAA national average, regular gasoline, Nov 12 2026

Here is what cheaper gas means for one fill-up.

At AAA's national average of $3.90 a gallon on Nov 12, a 15-gallon tank costs $58.50. A month earlier, at $4.36, the same tank cost $65.40.

That is $6.90 back per fill-up. Fill up once a week and it adds up to about $30 a month.

Your local price may be higher or lower than the national average.

My take: small per-gallon drops matter most to people who drive the most.

How often do you fill up?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, AAA national averages

Five dollars a day does not feel like much. Over time, it is.

Set aside $5 a day and you have about $150 after a month, $1,825 after a year, $9,125 after five years and $18,250 after ten. That is before any interest.

This is not about giving up coffee. It is about seeing what a small daily amount really adds up to.

My take: knowing the number makes the choice yours, either way.

What small daily spend would you redirect, if any?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, $5 a day, no interest

Your Social Security check is based on most of your working life, not the end of it.

The Social Security Administration uses your 35 highest-earning years, adjusted for wage growth over time. If you worked fewer than 35 years, the missing years count as zero.

That is why a few extra working years can raise a benefit for someone with gaps.

My take: it is worth checking your earnings record at ssa.gov. Mistakes happen.

Have you ever looked at your Social Security statement?

Source: Social Security Administration

#SocialSecurity #Retirement #MoneyMyths

A small monthly deposit builds a real cushion faster than most people expect.

Put $100 a month into savings earning 4% a year. After one year you have about $1,222. After three years, about $3,818. After five years, about $6,630, of which $6,000 is your own deposits.

4% is an example rate, not a quote. Rates vary by bank and change over time.

My take: an automatic transfer on payday does most of the work for you.

Do you have a savings transfer set up?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, 4% a year, compounded monthly

A longer car loan lowers the payment and raises the total.

On a $25,000 loan at 7% APR, 48 months costs about $599 a month and about $3,735 in interest. Stretch it to 72 months and the payment drops to about $426, but interest rises to about $5,688.

That is close to $2,000 more for the same car, and two extra years of payments.

My take: the monthly payment is the number dealers lead with. The total is the one that counts.

Which would you pick, and why?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, 7% APR, fixed monthly payments

Before income tax, two taxes come out of almost every paycheck.

You pay 6.2% for Social Security and 1.45% for Medicare, 7.65% in all. Your employer pays the same again on your behalf.

In 2026 the Social Security part stops after $184,500 of wages. Medicare has no cap, and high earners pay an extra 0.9% above $200,000.

My take: these are the taxes that fund the benefits most people will one day collect.

Have you ever looked closely at the lines on your pay stub?

Source: IRS; Social Security Administration
